pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Large, irregular polygonal dark regions with jagged, high-frequency edge gradients; the patches exhibit starburst-like protrusions at vertex points and vary from large, broad areas on the neck to more fragmented, smaller geometries on the lower flank.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Continuous network of light-colored interstitial pathways forming a complete topological graph; junction nodes are predominantly trifurcated with a consistent pixel width that maintains connectivity across the entire visible flank.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: Uniform, high-frequency mane profile along the neck with low-amplitude textural peaks providing a fine-grained silhouette against the out-of-focus background.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: A localized area of textural disruption and matted pelage is visible on the upper mid-flank, characterized by a flattened, darker appearance compared to the surrounding hair direction.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A small avian organism (red-billed oxpecker) is perched on the posterior dorsal ridge near the rump, creating a localized structural protrusion on the silhouette.
other_distinctive_markers: Partial occlusion of the primary subject's posterior region by the neck and head of a second giraffe in the background, showing a high-contrast reticulated pattern.
